label: build:fx
mission: EffectComposer chain (bloom tuned for HDR emissives, one cinematic pass with radial speed blur, chromatic aberration, vignette, grain, grade, impact flash, SMAA); pooled GPU particles (smoke, wet spray, sparks, nitro flames, skid marks); camera-following rain with splashes.

structured_report.summary:
I built the cinematic layer: post-processing, particles and rain. It all runs in the integrated game with no console errors, and core's src/core/effects.js already calls it.

POSTFX (src/fx/postfx.js): an EffectComposer with HalfFloat targets: RenderPass → UnrealBloomPass → AnamorphicStreakPass ('high' only) → CinematicPass → SMAA ('high') or FXAA ('low').
- **Bloom:** I replaced the bright pass with my own. It takes 4 bilinear taps (a 4x4 box) with Karis weighting so tiny lamps and glints don't shimmer, uses a soft knee, and clamps HDR luminance at 24. It also guards against NaN and Inf, so one bad pixel from any module can't black out the frame. The bloom chain runs at about half the CSS resolution whatever the pixel ratio (threshold 0.9, strength 0.42, radius 0.6).
- **Anamorphic streaks:** the bright pass is downsampled to a 1/8-wide, 1/4-tall target, then blurred horizontally 3 times with tap spacing of 1, 4 and 16 texels. Street lamps and headlights get the horizontal glare; it costs 4 tiny draws.
- **CinematicPass (one full-screen pass):**
  - radial speed blur toward the screen centre, with no blur in the central 30% and up to 12 taps ('low' 8). The tap count adapts to the blur length in pixels, and the taps are jittered.
  - chromatic aberration done with spectral tap weights inside the same blur loop, so it adds no extra texture fetches. It ramps with speed, nitro, impact and shake.
  - nitro adds a zoom punch, a pincushion warp and an activation pulse.
  - impact desaturates the image and flashes the exposure.
  - tone mapping follows renderer.toneMapping and toneMappingExposure, with the sRGB transfer, exactly like OutputPass.
  - after that, in display space: teal-shadow / warm-highlight split tone, saturation, an S-curve, black lift, vignette and animated film grain.

PARTICLES (src/fx/particles.js): pooled, at most 4 draw calls. Each layer hides itself when nothing is alive, so idle cost is 0.
- **Smoke:** an analytic GPU simulation. Spawn data is written once, and motion is solved in closed form in the vertex shader (drag, buoyancy, wind, rolling along the ground).
  - The billowy puff atlas is generated in code (metaballs eroded by noise), and older smoke blurs out through higher mip levels.
  - Billows get lit tops and shaded undersides from self-shadowing, with neon colour pick-up and a red glow from the tail lights.
  - Puffs fade where they meet the ground and fade out near the camera.
- **Spray:** one draw. Mist is drawn as billboards stretched by their motion relative to the camera, using soft mip-biased sprites and blending halfway between normal and additive so road reflections still show through. Droplets are additive streaks, motion-blurred relative to the camera.
- **"Hot" layer (one draw):**
  - sparks are simulated on the CPU with gravity, drag and a bounce on y=0; they are streaks that cool from white-yellow to red.
  - nitro flames use slots that stay attached to each exhaust: a blue body fading to violet, a white-hot core with shock diamonds, a nozzle glow, and a few embers.
  - everything is drawn as capsule sprites with pixel-accurate width (at least 0.8 px, faded rather than aliased).
- **Skid marks:** one draw. A 4000-segment ring buffer ('low' 2000) of joined quads per trackId, with a tread pattern and polygonOffset. Old marks fade out before they are overwritten, and marks fade with time.
- **CPU side:** typed arrays, no per-frame allocations, and only the changed ranges are uploaded. Emission is rate-based on frame time, spawn times are spread within the frame (so trails stay continuous at 300 km/h), and distant emitters spawn fewer, larger particles.

RAIN (src/fx/rain.js): 2 draws.
- **Streaks:** 14,000 instanced streaks ('low' 6000) wrapped in a 40x20x40 m box that follows the camera, all in the vertex shader.
  - Drops are fixed in world space with 3 fall-speed classes.
  - Each streak follows the drop's motion relative to the camera, so at speed rain rushes at the lens in radial streaks.
  - Near drops get bright refraction rims, and a few catch light or neon tints.
  - Drops inside the headlight beam are brighter, and drops fade at the box edges.
- **Splashes:** broken ripple rings plus tiny crown bounces, placed on a world-space tile grid using hashes so they stay put in the world, fully animated in the shader.

BENCH (dev/fx.html): a neon ring street with a planar-mirror wet road (bench only), a circling box car with every emitter, and lamp lights that follow the car. URL params: type=all|smoke|spray|sparks|nitro|skids|none, speed, nitro, impact, rain, drift, cam=chase|side|low|top|front, quality, nofx, hud, pause. window.__fx.breakdown() reports draw calls per part.

Bugs found and fixed while testing:
- quads collapsed by the segment-sprite winding were culled as back faces.
- flame slots were never ageing.
- a NaN from pow() of a tiny negative number flickered whole frames black through bloom; all pow() calls are now guarded, plus the NaN guard in postfx.
structured_report.contract_notes:
POSTFX
- **OutputPass is merged into CinematicPass.** It applies renderer.toneMapping, toneMappingExposure and outputColorSpace exactly like OutputPass. This saves one full-screen pass and keeps grading and grain in display space.
- **Pass order:** composer.passes = [RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, AnamorphicStreakPass (high only), CinematicPass, SMAAPass | FXAAPass].
- **Optional extras:** postfx.params (live tunables: bloomStrength, bloomThreshold, blurMax, caBase, vignette, grain, streak, exposure), bloomPass, cinematicPass, streakPass, renderPass, aaPass, dispose().
- **set():**
  - impact works either as a one-shot or as a per-frame decaying value. Postfx keeps the maximum and decays it internally at 5/s.
  - nitro is smoothed, and a rising edge above 0.5 triggers a zoom/warp punch.
  - shake adds chromatic aberration.
- **setSize(w, h):** re-reads renderer.getPixelRatio(), so core can also call composer.setPixelRatio first, as it already does. Bloom runs at about half the CSS resolution regardless of pixel ratio.

PARTICLES (interpretation)
- **velocity:** in emitSpray and emitSmoke, `velocity` is the unscaled world velocity of the emitting car or wheel. The module works out the fling, wake-drag and lift itself (spray mist inherits about 70–85% of it, droplets 60–85%, smoke 35%). Core already calls it this way.
- **Spray speed scaling:** emitSpray also scales by speed (full at 20 m/s and above, at least 15%), on top of the caller's intensity.
- **emitSparks(position, normal, intensity, velocity?):** the optional 4th argument is the car's velocity, which the sparks inherit. Core already passes it. Without it, sparks within 20 m of the camera inherit the camera's motion. Repeated calls within 0.12 s count as continuous scraping (rate-based); otherwise a call is a burst.
- **emitNitroFlame:** call once per exhaust every frame while it burns. Calls are matched to persistent slots by proximity (up to 24 flames at once), so each flame stays glued to its exhaust. A single call gives a burst of about 0.12 s, which suits backfire pops.
- **Optional extras:** clear() (core's EffectsDirector already uses it), group (the Group added to the scene), meshes {smoke, spray, hot, skids}, stats() (counts are pool high-water marks, not live particles), uniforms {wind, smokeColor, mistColor}, dispose().
- **Draw order:** renderOrder: skids -1 (ground layer), smoke 2, spray 3, hot 4. Rain streaks are 5 and splashes 0.

RAIN
- **update(dt, camera, velocity):** `velocity` is the world velocity of the camera or player. If it is omitted, it is estimated from camera motion.
- **Optional extras:**
  - setHeadlights(position, direction, on) lights rain in the player's beams. Until it is called, a chase-camera guess is used: beams start 8 m ahead of the camera and point along its forward direction.
  - setWind(x, z, fallSpeed), group, meshes, uniforms, dispose().
- **setIntensity(0..1):** thins drops and splashes evenly. At 0 the group is hidden.

REFLECTION (integrator)
- The world's planar reflection pass renders particles.group and rain.group too: up to 6 extra draws at half resolution.
- Smoke and spray in puddles look nice, but rain.group (and particles.group, if the budget is tight) can be pushed into environment's reflectHidden list to save fill rate.
known_issues: No true soft particles: there is no scene depth texture, so smoke and mist only fade softly where they meet the ground (y = 0) and near the camera. A large puff can show a hard edge where it cuts through a car body.

Smoke and mist are not lit by the scene's actual lights. Lighting is faked: shading from above, a neon tint that varies with world position, and a red glow near the tail lights. Core can retune it via particles.uniforms.smokeColor and mistColor.

Car module: at close range the player's headlight SpotLights blow out surfaces (for example nose-in against a barrier or wall), and bloom widens this into a large white glare. The bloom luminance clamp (24) limits single hot pixels but not a large overexposed area; the fix belongs in the headlight intensity and decay.
Rain is not occluded: it falls under the overpass and through roofs.

At race start, launch wheelspin from all 5 cars fills the screen with a lot of smoke. I lowered smoke rate and opacity and made smoke fade near the camera, but did not manage to re-capture the GO! moment, so the reduced version is unverified in-game.
The bench's mirror ground (three's Reflector) differs from the real road shader, so skid-mark contrast was judged in-game. On the dark wet road the marks show as subtle dark arcs.

The machine was heavily loaded during testing (load average 40–240, caused by the other agents' benches), so FPS numbers from the harness are not meaningful. Several screenshot runs were killed or caught a hot-reload mid-run and had to be repeated.
structured_report.perf_notes:
Measured in the bench with renderer.info (the bench also renders a mirror reflection, so its particle and rain numbers are doubled; per-view numbers below):
- **Post-processing:** 21 full-screen draws on 'high', 15 on 'low', plus the scene RenderPass.
  - Bloom is 13 draws (bright pass, 10 blur passes, composite, blend), all at half the CSS resolution or less ('low' 3/8).
  - The anamorphic streaks are 4 draws on targets of about 1/8 by 1/4 of the frame.
  - The cinematic pass is 1 full-resolution draw. Its blur loop is skipped where the blur is under 0.6 px (the centre at low speed) and uses about 1 tap per 2.5 px elsewhere, capped at 12.
  - SMAA is 3 full-resolution draws ('low': one FXAA pass).
- **Particles:** 0–4 draws (smoke, spray, hot, skids), each hidden when empty.
  - About 8k triangles submitted per view with every layer active; dead instances are culled in the vertex shader.
  - CPU per frame: an 800-spark loop, 24 flame slots, and range-limited buffer uploads. No allocations.
  - Pools ('high'): 2400 smoke, 3600 spray, 800 sparks plus 72 flame instances, 4000 skid segments. 'Low' halves them.
- **Rain:** 2 draws, 35k triangles on 'high' (14,000 streaks plus 1750 splashes x 2 quads) and about 15k on 'low'. No per-drop CPU work: the CPU updates 3 fall offsets and a few uniforms per frame.
- **Fill cost:** the main cost is the player's own spray mist and smoke near the camera. Mist blends halfway between normal and additive and smoke fades within about 0.4 m plus 0.9 x its size from the camera, which keeps overdraw down.
- **In-game totals (core's telemetry):** about 309–321 draw calls and about 1.6–1.7M triangles at about 58–59 fps, despite the machine load. FX accounts for roughly 21 post passes plus up to 6 draws in the main view, and up to 6 more in the world's half-resolution reflection pass.
